documents.unit: University of Arkansas AI Task Force / AI working groups (ai.uark.edu)
documents.title: Guidelines for Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The teaching section says student AI use 'is prohibited without the explicit permission of the course instructor', so the document's default for coursework is restrict. It also says faculty determine appropriate uses, which could be read as delegates, but the ban-unless-permitted default is set by the document itself.
documents.summary: Campus-wide acceptable-use guidelines covering ethics, integrity, teaching, research, tool approval, data classification and privacy. For coursework it says student AI use is prohibited without explicit instructor permission, while leaving each instructor to decide uses.

units.why: The purpose section says the university has a legislative 'obligation ... to address the authorized use of AI', which frames why the guidelines exist; it states scope and basis, so general and informs under the institution-wide framework type.

units.why: The passage says 'accountability for all final decisions ... resides with human employees ... regardless of any AI recommendation', so humans keep responsibility for decisions; P73 fits better than P46 because it is not limited to grading.
